Thanks for the details, Olivia — good signal. A few quick notes from the infra/serving side to help you fill the template: 

- GPU selection: H100 typically gives ~20–30% better throughput for long-context workloads compared to A100 for dense transformer inference (depends on model family and quantization). For mixed workloads where 8% are long-context (>2k tokens), H100 is cost-effective if you need tight latency SLOs. For purely short-context chat, A100 is often fine.
- Mapping TPS to concurrency: TPS * average latency (in seconds) ≈ concurrency. If your 200 TPS target has average end-to-end token latency target of 200–300ms, concurrency estimates are lower, but you must account for batching windows and KV cache warmups. For sizing, tell us your desired p99 latency SLO (e.g., <500ms) and whether you accept tail latency >1s during spikes.
- Token mix handling: long documents will dominate memory/KV usage. If 8% of requests hit 6k tokens, plan capacity with additional KV cache memory and possibly a separate pool for long-context workers.

I’ll prepare a rough 1-pass sizing based on the values I see in the sheet once Olivia shares the completed token/TPS numbers. If Thursday 7/2 10am PT works, I’ll join and bring a short sizing worksheet.

—Aditya

Perfect — thanks for the answers and token mix, Olivia. I’ve attached the overview and sizing template again. Please fill the following tabs in the sheet if possible: 

- "Traffic Profile": sustained TPS, burst TPS, peak window duration, traffic distribution over the hour/day.
- "Token Mix": prompt/response averages, percent long-context buckets (2k-4k, 4k-8k, >8k).
- "SLOs": p50/p95/p99 latency targets and acceptable tail latency during spikes.
- "Deployment Constraints": VPC requirements, IP allowlists, KMS/HSM needs.

Next steps: once you return the sheet, Aditya will produce a draft capacity plan (GPU counts/types, expected concurrency, estimated token cost) and we’ll schedule a follow-up to review.

Thanks — filling out the template now and will have a first pass by EOD. A couple quick notes from our side that might speed things up: 

- We currently prefer H100 if the cost delta is reasonable given the long-context needs.
- Our p99 target for interactive chat is <750ms; p95 <350ms. We accept occasional tail spikes to ~1.5s during the 5–10 minute bursts.
- Nightly indexing jobs can run on lower-priority GPUs; their token mix is mostly long (avg 4k context) but latency-insensitive.

Looking forward to the workshop — see you at 10.
